title: Set 294

sentences.ko: 내 폰이 자꾸 혼자 재부팅돼. 어제도 집주인한테 문자 쓰다 말고 그냥 꺼져 버려서, 지금 그 사람이 받았는지도 모르겠어.
sentences.text: My phone keeps restarting on its own. Like yesterday I was halfway through a text to my landlord and it just shut off, so now I don't even know if he got it.

alts.text: Ugh, my phone won't stop rebooting itself. Yesterday it died halfway through a text to my landlord, so now I've got no clue if he got it.
My phone continues to restart by itself. Yesterday, for example, I was in the middle of writing a message to my landlord when it suddenly shut off, so I do not know whether he received it.

sentences.note: **keeps restarting** 는 자꾸 재시작된다는 뜻으로, keep + ~ing 는 계속 반복되는 짜증나는 일을 말할 때 씁니다. **halfway through** 는 무언가를 하는 도중에, 반쯤 하다가라는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 회사에 어떤 사람이 자꾸 내가 한 걸 자기가 한 것처럼 가로채. 오늘 회의에서 또 그랬는데, 쪼잔해 보이기 싫어서 아무 말도 안 했거든. 근데 지금은 그냥 앉아서 나한테 너무 열받아.
sentences.text: This guy at work keeps taking credit for my stuff. He did it again in the meeting today, and I didn't say anything because I didn't want to look petty, but now I'm just sitting here mad at myself.

alts.text: Some guy at work keeps stealing credit for my stuff. Did it again today, and I let it go 'cause I didn't wanna look petty. Now I'm kicking myself.

A colleague of mine repeatedly takes credit for my work. He did so again in today's meeting, and I did not say anything because I did not wish to appear petty, but now I am simply sitting here, angry with myself.

sentences.note: **taking credit for** 는 남이 한 일의 공을 가로챈다는 뜻입니다. **petty** 는 사소한 일에 집착하는, 쪼잔한이라는 뜻이에요. **kicking myself** 는 내가 한 일이나 안 한 일 때문에 스스로를 탓한다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 나 그 드라마 진짜 좋아했는데, 작가 바뀌고 나서부터는 매주 그 개그가 그 개그야. 이미 네 시즌이나 본 게 아까워서 계속 보는 거야.
sentences.text: I used to love that show, but ever since they changed writers it's kind of the same jokes every week. I only keep watching because I've already put four seasons into it.

alts.text: I was so into that show, but since the new writers came in it's kinda the same jokes every week. Honestly I'm only still watching 'cause I'm four seasons deep.

I used to enjoy that show very much, but since the writers changed, it has been rather repetitive, with the same jokes every week. I continue watching only because I have already invested four seasons in it.

sentences.note: **ever since** 는 그때 이후로 쭉이라는 뜻입니다. **put four seasons into it** 은 네 시즌이나 들인 게 있다는 말로, 이미 쏟은 시간이 아까워 못 그만둔다는 느낌입니다.

sentences.ko: 그래, 그 타코집은 네 말이 맞았어. 음식 진짜 맛있더라. 근데 현금만 받는다는 말은 안 했잖아! 그래서 나 ATM 찾으러 길 따라 뛰어갔다 왔어. 데이트 상대는 그냥 앉아서 기다리고 있었고.
sentences.text: Okay, you were right about that taco place, the food was great. But you didn't tell me it was cash only, so I had to run down the street to find an ATM while my date just sat there waiting.

alts.text: Fine, you were right, that taco place was great. But you didn't say it was cash only! I had to run down the street hunting for an ATM while my date just sat there waiting.

I must admit that you were right about that taco restaurant; the food was excellent. However, you did not mention that it only accepted cash, so I had to hurry down the street to find a cash machine while my date sat there waiting.

sentences.note: **cash only** 는 현금만 받는다는 뜻으로 가게에서 자주 보는 표현입니다. **you were right about** ~ 는 ~에 대해서는 네 말이 맞았다고 인정할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 요즘 커피 한 잔에 6달러 받는 거 봤어? 예전엔 매일 아침 출근길에 하나씩 사 갔는데, 이제는 차라리 집에서 내려 마시고 좀 서글퍼하고 말래.
sentences.text: Have you seen they're charging six bucks for a coffee now? I used to grab one every morning on the way in, but at this point I'd rather just make it at home and be a little sad about it.

alts.text: Did you see coffee's six bucks now? I used to grab one every morning on my way in, but at this point I'll just make it at home and be kinda sad about it.

Have you noticed that they are now charging six dollars for a coffee? I used to buy one every morning on my way to work, but at this point I would rather make it at home, even if I am a little disappointed about it.

sentences.note: **grab one** 은 하나 사 간다, 가볍게 집어 간다는 뜻의 일상 표현입니다. **I'd rather** 는 차라리 ~하는 게 낫다는 뜻이고, **bucks** 는 달러를 편하게 부르는 말이에요.

reviewed: 2번 casual 이 text 와 끝부분(and now I'm just sitting here mad at myself)까지 거의 같아서, 더 짧고 축약된 구어로 바꾸고 끝을 kicking myself 로 고침
2번 한국어 '나 자신한테 화가 나' 가 번역투라 '나한테 너무 열받아' 로 고침
5번 한국어 '좀 슬퍼하는 게 나아' 가 어색해서 '좀 서글퍼하고 말래' 로 고침
